full_text:
सीकर में आज उमस और धूप से गर्मी बढ़ी:तापमान में बढ़ोतरी; इस साल मानसून की औसत बारिश से भी कम
- कॉपी लिंक
सीकर में आज तेज धूप निकली हुई है। आसमान साफ होने के कारण तापमान में भी बढ़ोतरी हो रही है। धूप बढ़ने की वजह से लोग गर्मी से परेशान हैं। इस बार मानसून की बारिश पूरी तरह कमजोर रही। मानसून की ट्रफ लाइन बार-बार शिफ्ट होने की वजह से सीकर में औसत से भी 8% कम बारिश हुई।
पिछले 4 दिन से मौसम ड्राई बना हुआ है और आज सुबह से तेज धूप के साथ उमस बरकरार है। गर्मी बढ़ने से दिन का तापमान भी बढ़ने की संभावना है। इस साल मानसून के फर्स्ट और सेकंड फेज में अच्छी बारिश नहीं हुई।
सीकर समेत शेखावाटी इलाके में अभी तक औसत से कम बारिश हुई है। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार- शेखावाटी में इस साल वेदर डिस्टर्बेंस और अल नीनो की वजह से बरसाती हवाओं की डायरेक्शन बदल गई।
मानसून की औपचारिक विदाई के बाद अब तेज बारिश का कोई पूर्वानुमान नहीं है। सीकर में 6 दिन पहले हुई बारिश के बाद अब फिर से गर्मी बढ़ गई है।
बात करें, सीकर के तापमान की तो सीकर जिले के फतेहपुर में स्थित कृषि अनुसंधान केंद्र के मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र पर आज सुबह का न्यूनतम तापमान 20.7 डिग्री दर्ज किया गया।
इससे पहले बुधवार को दिन का अधिकतम तापमान 38.5 डिग्री और न्यूनतम तापमान 20.0 डिग्री दर्ज किया गया था। सीकर जिला मुख्यालय पर आज बादलवाही नहीं होने से धूप में तेजी है और उमस बनी हुई है। इस कारण तापमान भी स्थिर बना हुआ है।
सीकर में कॉलेज गई 20 साल की युवती लापता: बेटे-बेटी के साथ महिला भी गायब, गहने लेकर चली गई; मोबाइल भी स्विच ऑफ
सीकर में शादी का झांसा देकर युवती से रेप: अश्लील फोटो-वीडियो वायरल करने की धमकी देकर किया ब्लैकमेल, पुलिस जांच में जुटी
आदर्श कॉलोनी में चार साल बाद सड़क का निर्माण: नवलगढ़ रोड पर पांच दिन से बंद स्ट्रीट लाइट हुई चालू
रिश्वत लेने वाले पटवारी को 4 साल की जेल: कोर्ट ने 35 हजार का जुर्माना भी लगाया; नामांतरण दर्ज करने के नाम पर 2 हजार मांगे थे

title: बदला मौसम का मिजाज: वेस्ट यूपी में रिमझिम बरसात ने दी गर्मी से राहत, तापमान में गिरावट; दो दिन बारिश के आसार - Amar Ujala

full_text:
बदला मौसम का मिजाज: वेस्ट यूपी में रिमझिम बरसात ने दी गर्मी से राहत, तापमान में गिरावट; दो दिन बारिश के आसार
वेस्ट यूपी में शनिवार सुबह से रिमझिम बारिश और ठंडी हवा से मौसम बदल गया। अगले दो दिन गरज-चमक के साथ मध्यम बारिश के आसार हैं, किसानों को सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी गई है।
विस्तार
पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश में शनिवार सुबह से रुक-रुककर हो रही रिमझिम बारिश से मौसम का मिजाज बदल गया। आसमान में बादल छाए रहने और ठंडी हवा के साथ हुई फुहारों ने पिछले कई दिनों से बढ़ रही गर्मी से राहत दिलाई। बारिश के चलते दिन के तापमान में भी गिरावट दर्ज की गई। मौसम विभाग ने शनिवार और रविवार को पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश में बारिश का पूर्वानुमान जारी किया है।
सुबह से रुक-रुककर होती रही बारिश
शनिवार सुबह से मेरठ और आसपास के क्षेत्रों में मौसम बदला हुआ नजर आया। कहीं हल्की बारिश हुई तो कहीं रिमझिम फुहारें पड़ती रहीं। बादल छाए रहने और ठंडी हवा चलने से मौसम खुशनुमा हो गया। सितंबर के अंतिम दिनों में हुई बारिश से लोगों को गर्मी से राहत मिली।
दो दिन गरज-चमक के साथ बारिश के आसार
सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल कृषि एवं प्रौद्योगिकी विश्वविद्यालय के मौसम वैज्ञानिक डॉ. यूपी शाही के अनुसार, शनिवार और रविवार को पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश में बादल छाए रहने के साथ गरज-चमक और मध्यम बारिश की संभावना है। इस दौरान तेज हवा भी चल सकती है।
दिन के तापमान में आएगी गिरावट
बारिश और बादलों के कारण दिन के तापमान में गिरावट आने की संभावना है। पिछले कई दिनों से मेरठ में दिन का तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास या इससे ऊपर बना हुआ था। बारिश के बाद तापमान कम होने से लोगों को दिन की गर्मी से राहत मिलने की उम्मीद है।
रविवार को भी बारिश के कारण मौसम अपेक्षाकृत ठंडा रह सकता है।सोमवार से मौसम में धीरे-धीरे सुधार होने की संभावना है। इसके बाद तापमान में फिर बढ़ोतरी हो सकती है।
किसानों के लिए बारिश राहत भी, चुनौती भी
हल्की बारिश खेतों के लिए फायदेमंद हो सकती है। जिन खेतों में मिट्टी में नमी कम थी, वहां बारिश से नमी बढ़ेगी। धान, गन्ना और अन्य खरीफ फसलों को इससे लाभ मिल सकता है। जिन किसानों ने सिंचाई की तैयारी की थी, उन्हें फिलहाल पानी देने की जरूरत कम हो सकती है।
हालांकि तेज बारिश और हवा की स्थिति में खेतों में पानी भरना नुकसानदायक हो सकता है। पकने की ओर बढ़ रही फसलों और खेतों में खड़ी सब्जियों को विशेष सावधानी की जरूरत है। किसानों को मौसम की स्थिति को देखते हुए सिंचाई और फसल कटाई से जुड़े काम करने की सलाह दी गई है।

Happy Saturday! Finally, some good weather to talk about!
If you’ve been ready for a break from the heat, this weekend is delivering. We’re waking up to cooler, fall-like temperatures, and we’re going to keep them around through the weekend. High temperatures today and Sunday will stay in the 70s, with overnight lows dropping into the 40s and 50s. So yes, you can finally grab that jacket in the morning and actually have a reason to wear it!
High pressure and northerly flow will keep plenty of sunshine around through the weekend, with no rain in the forecast. Now, this cool stretch won’t last forever. As our pattern shifts next week, winds will turn more southerly, and temperatures will start climbing back into the 80s by Tuesday. This is still pleasant, as we just endured a 50-day streak in the 90s. We’ll stay warmer than normal for much of next week, but there is another change coming. By the latter part of the week, rain chances could return as another system moves in.
But for now, enjoy it. Cool mornings, comfortable afternoons, sunshine, and dry weather. After the heat we’ve had, I think we’ve earned this one!

title: El Niño’s heat could cause 451,000 additional deaths worldwide between October 2026 and February 2027 - The Tanzania Times

full_text:
Just as many East African countries are bracing for excessive rains, floods and landslides, new reports claim that El Niño’s heat could cause 451,000 additional deaths worldwide.
Even as many East African countries will suffer from the related rains instead, at least three states on the continent will be badly hit by the heat.
Already heavy downpours have already started precipitating in parts of Kenya, Uganda and DR Congo.
However, elsewhere around the global excessive heat seems to be the real problem.
In Africa, DR Congo, Nigeria and Sudan are predicted to suffer from El-Nino heat attacks.
At least 60,000 people may face serious problems on the continent due to rising temperatures.
Land temperatures around the world could average roughly 2.1°F (1.2°C) above the 1996–2025 baseline in the coming months, largely because of the El-Nino phenomenon.
A Climate Impact Lab report estimates 451,000 additional heat-related deaths that are likely to occur during the first part of this El Niño, including approximately 239,000 between September 2026 and February 2027.
The threat extends beyond brief, headline-making heat waves.
Months of persistently higher temperatures can place a cumulative strain on health.
Researchers say that sustained exposure can produce a substantial death toll even without a single dramatic weather event.
El Niño is suspected to develop when waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific become unusually warm.
The resulting changes in atmospheric circulation influence heat and rainfall far beyond the Pacific.
This event is adding to temperatures already elevated by human-driven climate change.
Researchers say the coming conditions could resemble those that global warming makes typical in roughly 20 years.
The largest tolls are expected in the Global South. Over the coming months, researchers project approximately:
• Nigeria: 31,400 additional deaths
• Indonesia: 19,300
• Sudan: 17,500
• India: 15,800
• Brazil: 13,300
• Democratic Republic of Congo: 10,000
The report also projects a combined 19,400 additional deaths across the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, and Cambodia.
The analysis combines temperature forecasts with methods linking temperature and mortality across thousands of regions. Its estimates concern heat and exclude additional deaths from floods, droughts, wildfires, and food shortages.
These are projections, not confirmed deaths or an unavoidable outcome. The report itself had not yet undergone peer review, according to environmental experts.
Its regional detail is intended to help governments direct resources where they could save the most lives.
Earlier heat warnings, cooling centers, drinking-water access, outdoor-worker protections, and additional medical staffing could reduce the toll. Researchers say targeted action could prevent tens of thousands of deaths.

Three lions that died at Tokyo’s Tama Zoological Park, from left, Mugi, Ichigo and Ruena (Provided by Tokyo Zoological Park Society)
Lions in sub-Saharan Africa inhabit savannas, which are arid regions in tropical areas, and are seemingly well-suited to surviving the heat.
However, three lionesses kept at Tama Zoological Park in the western Tokyo city of Hino died possibly due to an extreme heat wave that started in mid-July.
An expert said their tragic deaths are related to rapid increases in temperature and high humidity.
The three lionesses ranged in age from 3 to 15.
Necropsies performed by park veterinarians revealed that all three suffered from systemic dehydration and multiple organ failure.
A record-breaking heat wave was blamed for their deaths.
According to the Tokyo metropolitan government, which oversees the zoo, two lions showed symptoms including loss of appetite and decreased activity, prompting staff to provide them with treatment.
Of 16 lions kept at the zoo, a total of 10, including the three that died, eventually developed similar symptoms.
Hideaki Karaki, a professor emeritus of veterinary medicine at the University of Tokyo, said that their deaths may have been caused by two misfortunes.
The first is that their basic stamina was weakened because of the heat.
In Tokyo, temperatures rose rapidly from mid-July.
According to the Japan Meteorological Agency, the average highest temperature in early July was 27.6 degrees at an observation point in Hachioji, which is adjacent to Hino.
But the figure rose to 35.2 degrees later that month.
“The temperature rises and drops slowly in savannas,” Karaki said. “There is enough time to adapt to the heat.”
The sudden surge in temperature robbed them of strength, he added.
The second is that the high humidity made it difficult for the lions to regulate their body temperature.
Lions don’t sweat because they are a cat species that has few perspiration glands. Instead, they breathe to let moisture in the respiratory tract evaporate to lower their body temperatures.
But unlike savannas, Tokyo is more humid.
“Because evaporation was insufficient no matter how hard they breathed, they might have been unable to reduce their body temperature,” Karaki said.
“It’s not a problem just for lions, and we should make it a lesson for humans, too,” he continued. “It’s hot enough to kill animals (that live in tropical areas). Unlike lions, we humans can defend ourselves, so I want everyone to be on the alert for heatstroke.”

The system is expected to bring heavy rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds to several regions, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warning of waterlogging and flooding in vulnerable areas.
Uttarakhand remains the biggest concern, with a red alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall and the possibility of cloudbursts, landslides and mudslides. Several parts of Uttar Pradesh are also likely to witness intense rainfall over the next two days.

Mumbai: The Maharashtra government has declared drought in 265 of the state’s 368 talukas after they met the prescribed criteria under Trigger-1 of the state’s drought assessment framework.
The government issued a Government Resolution (GR) on Saturday, directing district collectors to conduct panchnamas to assess crop losses in the affected areas.
The state uses a three-stage trigger matrix based on meteorological and other parameters to assess drought conditions. The declaration follows a consolidated preliminary report submitted to the government on the situation across Maharashtra.
The drought-affected talukas are spread across 32 districts. Yavatmal has the highest number at 16, followed by Jalgaon with 15, and Ahilyanagar, Nanded, Amravati and Nagpur with 14 each.
The government has announced several relief measures, including a waiver of land revenue, restructuring of crop loans and a halt to their recovery. Farmers will also receive relief on electricity bills for agricultural pumps, while students from affected areas will be exempted from school and college fees.
The state will undertake rural employment programmes to generate jobs locally in the drought-hit areas. Drinking-water tankers will be deployed wherever necessary, while work on providing electricity connections to agricultural pumps will continue.
The government will also ensure foodgrain supplies to farmers and agricultural labourers dependent on farming for their livelihoods.
Fodder camps will be established to support livestock in affected areas. The government will also undertake check-dam development works and prepare plans to ensure adequate drinking water for people and livestock.

Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services has warned of 'Kallakkadal' or swell wave phenomenon from September 26-28 and urged coastal residents to exercise caution.
Thiruvananthapuram: The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) has issued a red alert across all coastal districts in Keralam over the possibility of high waves and the swell wave phenomenon, locally known as 'Kallakkadal'. Accordingly, the authorities have urged coastal residents and the fishing community to remain alert for the impending rough sea conditions.
The red alert remains effective from 2.30 am on September 26 until 2.30 am on September 28. During this period, waves reaching heights of one to one-and-a-half meters are expected to lash the Kerala coast. Residents of vulnerable areas have been advised to relocate to safer locations as low-lying coastal areas face a significant threat of waterlogging and severe sea incursion.
The 'Kallakkadal' phenomenon refers to a sudden and unexpected sea surge that occurs without any prior atmospheric warning. This condition is triggered by massive waves formed by strong winds in distant oceans, which eventually crash onto the shores. These unpredictable waves can cause widespread destruction along the coast, even in the complete absence of local winds or rainfall.
Special vigilance is required across various regions in the nine coastal districts of the state. The warning covers the stretches from Kappil to Pozhiyoor in Thiruvananthapuram, Alappad to Edava in Kollam, and Chellanam to Azheekal jetty in Alappuzha. The alert also extends from Munambam fishing harbour to Maruvakkad in Ernakulam, Attupuram to Kodungallur in Thrissur, and Kadalundi Nagaram to Palappetty in Malappuram. Furthermore, a high alert has been declared from Chombala fishing harbour to Ramanattukara in Kozhikode, Valapattanam to New Mahe in Kannur, and Kunjathur to Kottakunnu in Kasaragod.
In addition to Kerala, warnings regarding high waves and the swell wave phenomenon have been issued for the Lakshadweep islands and the coastal regions of Tamil Nadu, specifically Kanyakumari, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, and Tirunelveli.
As the sea surge is likely to intensify, people residing in vulnerable zones must shift to safer accommodations in compliance with official directives. The launching of small boats and vessels into the sea must be completely avoided during this period. Authorities have emphasised that both launching and docking fishing vessels are highly dangerous during swell waves, and such activities should be strictly prohibited while the sea remains rough.
All beach-centric tourism activities will stay suspended until the warning is officially withdrawn by the INCOIS. The public is strictly advised to avoid beach visits and water-based recreational activities in coastal areas. Fishermen must ensure their vessels are securely moored at the harbours, maintaining a safe distance between boats to prevent collision damage. Additionally, fishing equipment must be safely stored, and coastal communities should remain highly vigilant against potential coastal erosion.

Punjab Newsline | Chandigarh
India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for Chandigarh for Saturday and Sunday, warning of the possibility of heavy rainfall over the weekend.
According to the weather department, the expected rain spell could bring a significant change in weather conditions and may mark the beginning of the monsoon's withdrawal from the region. Residents have been grappling with hot and humid conditions in recent days, with Friday's maximum temperature recorded at 32 degrees Celsius and the minimum at 26 degrees Celsius.
Meteorologists said that rainfall is likely to lower daytime temperatures, providing relief from the prevailing humidity. A drop in temperature could also lead to a mild chill during early morning and nighttime hours.
Chandigarh has received 697.6 mm of rainfall so far this monsoon season, which is 17.2 percent below the seasonal average. Despite the overall rainfall deficit, the city has witnessed several spells of intense rain during the season.
The weather department has forecast continued rainfall activity over the next two days. Following this wet spell, the southwest monsoon is expected to begin its gradual retreat from the region, bringing a transition in weather patterns and cooler conditions.

Heavy rain in MP raises river levels, submerges bridges:9 Bargi gates opened; water also released from Johila, Bilgaon dams
- Copy link
Heavy rain over the past three days in Dindori and Umaria has raised the water levels of the Narmada and its tributaries. The bridge at Jogi Tikariya in Dindori is submerged, disrupting traffic on National Highway 45 between Jabalpur and Amarkantak for the past seven hours.
Two gates of the Bilgaon Dam in Shahpura, Dindori, have been opened. In Umaria, four gates of the Johila Dam at the Sanjay Gandhi Thermal Power Station have been opened by two metres each to release water.
All schools in Satna, Maihar and Umaria have been declared closed on September 26 as a precautionary measure for students. The decision was taken due to waterlogging and continuous rain.
Five gates of the Bargi Dam were opened on Friday to regulate the water level. However, the inflow continued, prompting authorities to open four more gates on Saturday.
Water is now being released through all nine gates of the Bargi Dam. Due to the discharge, the water level at Narmada ghats has risen by around 6–8 feet from the current level.
Rain likely to continue in eastern MP
Weather expert Shailendra Kumar Nayak said Madhya Pradesh’s weather has become active again in the last week of September. Although the intensity of the deep depression is gradually weakening, its north-northwestward movement and associated moisture are sufficient to sustain rainfall in eastern Madhya Pradesh.
The next 48 hours are therefore particularly important. The administration, farmers and residents should keep an eye on local weather alerts. People should also avoid unnecessary travel near rivers, streams, bridges and low-lying areas.
PHOTOS…
5 days left for monsoon withdrawal
The southwest monsoon period in MP runs from June 1 to September 30. This means five days are left for the monsoon to withdraw. The withdrawal is expected to begin in the coming days. The monsoon has already withdrawn from several districts of Rajasthan.
State rainfall 2.2 inches below normal
According to the IMD, Madhya Pradesh has received 880.5 mm (34.7 inches) of rainfall so far. This is 2.2 inches below the normal rainfall of 36.9 inches (937.9 mm) for this period.
Overall, the state has received 6% less rainfall than normal. Rainfall in the eastern region is around normal, while the western region has received 11% less than average. Jabalpur, Rewa, Sagar and Shahdol divisions in eastern MP have recorded rainfall close to normal.
Balaghat, Chhindwara, Dindori, Damoh, Jabalpur, Katni, Narsinghpur, Pandhurna, Mandla, Rewa, Sagar and Seoni have received 4% to 21% less rainfall than normal. The figures have improved significantly over the past week, with rainfall reaching the normal level on Friday.
In the western region, Alirajpur, Ashoknagar, Betul, Dewas, Dhar, Harda, Indore, Jhabua, Khandwa, Mandsaur, Morena, Narmadapuram, Neemuch, Barwani, Raisen, Ratlam, Sehore, Shajapur, Ujjain and Vidisha have received 8% to 50% less rainfall than average.
These 23 districts have received above-average rainfall
According to the IMD, above-average rainfall has been recorded in Anuppur, Chhatarpur, Maihar, Mauganj, Niwari, Panna, Satna, Shahdol, Sidhi, Singrauli, Tikamgarh, Umaria, Agar-Malwa, Bhind, Bhopal, Burhanpur, Datia, Guna, Gwalior, Khargone, Rajgarh, Sheopur and Shivpuri.

State activates “Trigger-1” after rainfall deficit of over 25% combined with prolonged dry spell across 32 districts
The Maharashtra government has declared drought conditions in 265 of the state’s 358 talukas, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said Saturday, covering close to 75 per cent of the state following an assessment of rainfall, water availability and crop conditions.
A government resolution formalising the declaration was issued late Friday, with a series of relief measures set to follow across the affected areas.
The trigger behind the decision
The state activated “Trigger-1” under its Drought Management Code and manual for drought management, first framed in 2016 and updated in 2020. Trigger-1 is the first stage in Maharashtra’s drought-response framework, activated when a region sees a rainfall deficit of more than 25 per cent combined with a prolonged dry spell of at least 21 days.
A report from the state’s Agriculture Commissioner found drought-like conditions across the 265 talukas spanning 32 districts, driven by rainfall shortfalls and related factors. State data showed an overall rainfall deficit of 18.8 per cent, with the state receiving 755.9 mm of rainfall between June and September 18 against an average of 932.3 mm, amid El Niño conditions. The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division — which includes Dharashiv and five other Marathwada districts — was among the worst hit, recording a 30.8 per cent deficit, while the Pune and Nashik divisions also saw shortfalls of around 30 per cent.
Relief measures announced
Fadnavis announced a package of relief measures for the affected talukas, including restructuring of crop loans, concessions on land revenue, and a deferment of recovery on agriculture-related loans, with no coercive action to be taken against farmers during the relief period. Electricity concessions have also been expanded: pumps up to 7.5 horsepower were already exempt from bills, and the government has now extended that exemption to higher-capacity pumps as well.
A separate government resolution is expected on financial assistance for crop losses in the 265 declared talukas, to be issued after the prescribed procedure is completed. Fadnavis has also directed district collectors to set up 24-hour war rooms to coordinate relief operations and ensure the measures are implemented promptly, with the administration placed on alert to monitor drinking-water availability, agricultural losses and fodder supply.
The declaration follows Fadnavis’s recent visits to drought-affected parts of the state.

*Immediate Assistance from Our Government, Considering Farmers’ Distress.
*Losses Estimated at Over Rs.40,000 Crore;Final Relief Amount to Be Decided After Central Team’s Assessment: DyCM.
The State Government has decided to provide an input subsidy of ₹2,500 to each farmer in the first phase to extend immediate assistance to farmers affected by drought.
Around 45 to 50 lakh farmers will benefit from this assistance,at an estimated cost of around ₹1,250 crore to the State exchequer.
Although NDRF assistance from the Union Government is awaited,our Government is providing immediate relief considering the distress faced by farmers,Deputy Chief Minister and Revenue Minister,Dr.G.Parameshwara said.
Speaking to the media near his residence in Sadashivanagar today, he said the State Government is already extending various forms of assistance to farmers.
Around Rs.22,000 crore is being provided as power subsidy to supply free electricity to agricultural pump sets.
The first-phase assistance of ₹1,250 crore is not a small amount. Further measures will be taken in the coming days based on the relief received from the Union Government,he said.
The total loss caused by drought in the State is likely to exceed ₹40,000 crore.
The first memorandum has already been submitted to the Union Government,and additional memoranda will be submitted in the coming days.
After preparing the final estimate of the total loss,the State will submit to the Centre the amount of relief required under the NDRF guidelines,he said.
Dr.Parameshwara clarified that further relief measures will be decided based on the manner in which the Union Government extends assistance to the State.At this stage,it is not possible to make any commitment regarding a revised relief amount.
The Union Government has already written to the State Government regarding sending a team,including an IAS officer,to assess the drought situation.
The date of the team’s visit has not yet been fixed.Once the Central team visits the State and assesses the drought situation and losses in accordance with its guidelines,there will be greater clarity on the extent of further relief,he said.
Regarding taking an all-party delegation to Delhi on drought relief,he said the Chief Minister and he had already clarified the matter in the Legislative Assembly.
An all-party meeting will be held,everyone will be taken into confidence,and the delegation will be taken to Delhi, he said.
The delegation will meet the Prime Minister,Union Home Minister and Union Agriculture Minister and explain Karnataka’s drought situation and the distress faced by farmers.
If Opposition members are willing to join, the Government is ready to take them along as well.
The date of the delegation’s visit to Delhi has not yet been fixed,he said.
Response to the protest seeking an increase in the honorarium for persons with disabilities:
Referring to the protest by persons with disabilities in Ramanagara seeking an increase in their honorarium, he said the concerned department must prepare a proposal and place it before the Cabinet.
The Chief Minister is also the Finance Minister.If the proposal is discussed with him and brought before the Cabinet,everyone will extend their cooperation,he said.
